output.brief: The remote promotion gap is mostly a time-in-level effect, not a location effect. Policy requires 18 months in level to be nominated. Only 32% of remote staff meet that, against 74% of office staff, so the remote group is newer. Among eligible people, the rates are nearly the same: 20.0% remote and 21.1% office. Nomination rates (28% vs 29%) and committee approval rates (71% vs 74%) are also close. The gap appears in every job family because the tenure mix differs in every family, not because of proximity bias. Caveat: only 110 remote employees are eligible, so a real difference of a few points can't be ruled out. I did not test whether remote staff get fewer high-visibility assignments, or whether they leave at a higher rate. Manager comments hint at the first, and the second is unmeasured. Recommendation: don't announce the three-day office rule. It would penalise people hired on home-based contracts and rests on a misread comparison. Report promotion rates for eligible staff only, and re-check at the FY2027 cycle. Meanwhile, look at assignment allocation and attrition data. Confidence is moderately high.
